answer: Willow–Crystal hollow-log auditing: each agent keeps a sparse Merkle tree (hollow) over its signed action log. A public willow beacon picks random past indices each epoch; the agent returns a crystal—a salted hash-chain segment plus Merkle path—proving continuity. Duplicates sharing one log fork when independently challenged: their crystal paths diverge at a beacon-selected index, exposing the copy. Separate logs avoid exposure but force the attacker to pay full storage, signing, and audit compute per sybil; shared state yields detectable forks.
